title: Voz pasiva y se pasiva en textos históricos

sections.content: Historical writing uses two passive constructions almost interchangeably: *ser* + participle (*fue descifrada*), which often names who did the action with *por*, and the *se* passive (*se talló*, *se han identificado*), which drops the doer entirely and reads more naturally when the agent doesn't matter. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: La escritura maya fue descifrada en gran parte gracias al trabajo del lingüista soviético Yuri Knórozov.
items.english: Maya writing was deciphered largely thanks to the work of Soviet linguist Yuri Knórozov.

items.spanish: Durante mucho tiempo se pensó que las ciudades del sur fueron simplemente abandonadas por guerras o mala administración.
items.english: For a long time it was thought that the southern cities were simply abandoned due to wars or poor administration.

items.spanish: En Copán se talló la escalinata jeroglífica más larga conocida.
items.english: In Copán, the longest known hieroglyphic stairway was carved.

items.spanish: Se han identificado más de ochocientos glifos distintos.
items.english: More than eight hundred distinct glyphs have been identified.

sections.content: Reach for *ser* + participle when you want to name who did it (*fue descifrada por Knórozov*); reach for *se* + verb when the doer is unknown, irrelevant, or already obvious from context (*se talló*, *se han identificado*). Both are more common in formal historical writing than in everyday speech.
